claims.text: Applying an AlCrTiZrMo HEA coating will improve surface hardness, wear resistance, and oxidation protection relative to an uncoated component.
Laser cladding is a suitable deposition method for an AlCrTiZrMo HEA coating.
Annealing the AlCrTiZrMo coating will promote formation of a protective oxide layer.
The coating is intended to operate in high-temperature, oxidizing, and tribocorrosive environments involving thermal shock and corrosive media.
The HEA high-entropy effect and induced lattice distortion facilitate formation of a fine, dense microstructure.
Annealing promotes formation of a stable composite oxide such as ZrTiO4.
The composite oxide layer acts as a barrier to further oxidation.
The composite oxide layer minimizes wear.
The multicomponent AlCrTiZrMo coating inherently has enhanced hardness and oxidation resistance.
A dense high-temperature oxide layer seals the surface against corrosive attack and mechanical erosion.
A refined coating microstructure increases hardness and wear resistance.
The coating may increase microhardness by approximately 30–40% relative to the untreated baseline.
The coating will produce a notably lower wear rate than the untreated baseline.
The coating will improve oxidation resistance under thermal-shock conditions.
Untreated components generally have lower hardness, greater wear or degradation, and poorer oxidation performance in aggressive high-temperature environments.

The performance enhancement should persist during continuous exposure up to approximately 800 °C in oxidizing and corrosive saline or molten-salt environments, provided coating adhesion and integrity are maintained.
Long-term cyclic durability under repeated thermal shock and adhesion across different substrates remain uncertain.
A controlled comparison will use coated and untreated coupons made from the same substrate material.
The hypothesis will be falsified if hardness improves by less than 20%, wear rate falls by less than 50%, or substantial coating degradation occurs under the specified tests.
